details: Bitcoin has experienced a volatile period, testing lower support levels, as soaring US Treasury yields and a strong dollar put significant pressure on risk assets, including cryptocurrencies. US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw nearly $1 billion in outflows within two trading days, leading to cautious market sentiment. The probability of an interest rate hike in 2026 has surged, further impacting risk appetite.
title: Bitcoin Faces Pressure Amid Rising US Treasury Yields and ETF Outflows

details: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is reportedly planning to unveil an "innovation exemption" for trading tokenized or digital versions of securities as early as this week. This move by the Trump administration aims to create a new regulatory pathway for trading shares on crypto platforms, potentially outside traditional exchanges. This could significantly integrate traditional finance with blockchain technology.
title: SEC Prepares Framework for Trading Tokenized Stocks

details: Senator Elizabeth Warren has accused the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) of illegally approving national trust charters for several crypto firms, including those linked to Coinbase and Ripple. Warren argues that these firms may be operating like banks without adhering to full banking regulations, posing risks to consumers and the broader financial system.
title: Senator Warren Challenges OCC's Crypto Trust Charter Approvals

details: Investors are awaiting the release of the April Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting minutes on May 20-21, 2026. These minutes will offer deeper insights into the Federal Reserve's policy stance regarding persistent inflation concerns and the path of quantitative tightening (QT). Any hints of a hawkish outlook or slower liquidity easing could impact cryptocurrency markets.
title: FOMC Meeting Minutes Release Eyed for Fed's Inflation Stance

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has affirmed its support for tokenization, recognizing its potential to enhance efficiency and transparency in financial markets. However, the ECB emphasizes the need for strict rules and has endorsed a proposal to move the direct supervision of "systemically important" crypto firms and cross-border trading platforms to the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA). This aims to curb financial risks and market fragmentation.
title: ECB Supports Tokenization but Calls for Centralized EU Oversight

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has issued a warning that the rapid expansion of tokenized finance and stablecoins could fundamentally reshape global financial markets, introducing new systemic risks. Key concerns include market fragmentation due to a lack of common standards, accelerated shock propagation in highly interconnected systems, challenges in cross-border resolution, and the erosion of monetary sovereignty in emerging economies.
title: IMF Warns of Systemic Risks from Tokenized Finance and Stablecoins

details: The cryptocurrency market exhibited mixed signals, with a majority of tokens experiencing a decline on May 20, reflecting bearish sentiment. However, some speculative altcoins, such as "Banana For Scale," saw significant surges, indicating a growing risk appetite among certain investors. Additionally, Ethereum exchange-traded funds (ETFs) attracted massive inflows.
title: Crypto Market Shows Mixed Performance, Altcoins See Surges
